newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU plays down Finnish 1996 deficit overshoot.
newsitem.headline: EU plays down Finnish 1996 deficit overshoot.

text.p: A European Commission official played down the significance of an upward revision of Finland's 1996 budget deficit to 3.1 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) on Monday, saying Helsinki's commitment to meet the EMU criteria was not in doubt.
"This shouldn't be exaggerated," the official said, stressing that Finland had made major efforts in recent years to bring down its budget deficit.
"Its commitment to strong convergence towards the criteria shouldn't in any way be questioned."
Finland was expected to notify the Commission in September about the revised data, after which the EU executive will assess the situation, she said.
The Finnish finance ministry earlier said the 1997 public sector deficit in relation GDP would be inside the three-percent limit goal for economic and monetary union (EMU) despite the 1996 overshoot.

State secretary Raimo Sailas told Reuters in Helsinki that even in a worst-case scenario, the 1997 deficit would be safely within the EMU target. The ministry had not changed its 1997 forecast of a deficit of 1.4 percent of GDP. Countries aiming to join EMU will be judged by their 1997 performance.
Sailas and an official at Statistics Finland (SF) attributed the recent revision of the 1996 deficit to 3.1 percent of GDP from 2.6 percent mainly to non-recurring factors.
Finland has repeatedly said it will meet the entry criteria and intends to be among the founders of the new euro.
